qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Ductile deformation accumulates dislocations at the interfaces of δ-ferrite band and tempered martensite lamellar; hardness difference causes stress concentration, initiating cracks. Once formed, cracks are captured by δ-ferrite and propagate into/along the δ-ferrite band forming second cracks like deep valleys (observed in the QA-740 fracture, Fig. 6c).

interface_notes.value: The coarse δ-ferrite grains have deficient high-angle grain boundaries, so microcracks propagate as cleavage within δ-ferrite; the soft δ-ferrite can blunt propagating cracks, giving high cracking resistance.

phase_evolution.value: During annealing at 740 °C reverted austenite nucleated and grew at martensite lath gaps with diffusion of C and Mn into austenite and Al into martensite/ferrite; block boundaries were gradually replaced by AG boundaries as annealing temperature increased. No carbides precipitated at 740 °C and no new martensite formed on air cooling (unlike QA-800).

slip_behavior.value: Dislocation gliding initiates sequentially in ferrite and austenite (soft phases) then tempered martensite; strain-induced martensite acts as obstacle to dislocation glide and site of dislocation accumulation. Work hardening of QA-740 is governed by the three-stage WHR behaviour with TRIP dominating stage III.

source.reason: Discussion of deformation behaviour describes dislocation accumulation at δ-ferrite band / tempered martensite lamellar interfaces, second cracks in the QA-740 fracture, and phase evolution (reverted austenite, absence of carbides at 740 °C), all applying to the QA-740 specimen.

comparison_metric.value: highest product of strength and elongation (PSE) and maximum uniform elongation among HR, IQ-1050 and QA-620/680/740/800

performance_notes.value: QA-740 had the highest PSE ~45.2 GPa % and the maximum uniform elongation ~62.4 % of all treatment states. More than half of the austenite in QA-740 participated in the TRIP effect, causing the best total elongation. QA-740 showed the highest k value (~1.47, high TRIP activity, lower austenitic stability) together with QA-800. All QA specimens exhibited low yield-to-tensile ratio and could substitute for TRIP 580T/400Y (or 590T/400Y) high strength automobile plates per SAE J2745-2007.
